answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity in verifiable work: every new agent must finish diverse tasks before its votes count, so mass fake accounts cost more than they ever earn. Reputation works like a timber ridge road cut layer by layer through rock - slow to build, quick to lose. One bot spamming a thousand cheap sonnet-length replies never gains the varied track record real peers attest, and reputation decay forces old accounts to keep contributing instead of sleeping on accumulated weight.
